summary: This article explains how falcons use sharp eyes, fast dives, and strong talons to hunt, and why falconry is an important tradition in Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Read the title “Falcons: The Fastest Hunters” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: an animal that hunts and eats other animals
the fast, steep dive a falcon makes when it attacks
how well a person or animal can see

challengeTerms.def: the speed of something moving in a certain direction
shaped so that air or water flows past it easily
a small, rounded bump on a plant or an animal's body

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that falcons are the most amazing birds in the world? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why falconry is important to many families in Saudi Arabia.
struggling: Pre-teach predator, stoop, and eyesight with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use velocity, streamlined, and tubercle in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
